expectation_provenance_labels.static-derived; not observed reference o: derived for the target build without running it, from evidence reviewed before sanitization
expectation_provenance_labels.extracted execution; not observed refere: the deciding binary64 values of the case (the conversion result, or the rounded beat and the beat bounds that decide the outcome) were computed by the original program's x86_64 code for this case's inputs, run on a Linux x86_64 host outside the application; for a conversion, that code computed the step between seconds and beats, and the division of a position in frames by the sample rate and the multiplication of a result by it are static-derived and exact for every case with this label; the grid rounding ran in another part of the original program that rounds a beat with the same operations as the add and the marker lookup (static-derived); the macOS arm64 build is inferred to compute the same; opening, the comparisons of the deciding values, the call's other checks and the sample rate are static-derived
expectation_provenance_labels.computed by extracted-execution rules; n: computed for this case's inputs with the binary64 operation sequences that extracted execution of the original x86_64 code confirmed on other inputs; this input was not run; otherwise as static-derived

stated_assumptions: The base set, whose device lists are empty, opens in the target build. Its structure follows static-derived rules (every case).
Marker times are held as binary64 values read by the decimal rule of REQ-WARP-MARKERS-002 (every case).

The sample length that add_warp_marker compares with is the duration of the clip's sample, 3 s (cases 021 to 032, 052 to 055 and 059 to 061). Every add whose sample time lies in the sample stays at least 0.5 s before its end, and the 900,000 s of case 024 lies beyond it whether it is counted in seconds, milliseconds or frames.
The sample rate that both conversions use is the rate of the clip's sample, 8,000 Hz, which the clip also stores (cases 039 to 051).
An add or remove whose checks all pass raises no further error (cases 022, 031, 032, 035, 038, 052, 054, 058, 059, 061 and 063).
The marker lookup of REQ-WARP-MARKERS-015 clause 7 behaves as stated (cases 033 to 038, 056 to 058, 062 and 063).
The macOS arm64 build computes the conversions, the grid rounding and the beat bounds with the same binary64 operations as the x86_64 build (cases 039 to 060).
A conversion made right after opening uses the marker list held after opening (cases 039 to 051).

inputs_without_expectation: SecTime or BeatTime text starting, after spaces and a sign, with 0x, inf or nan; the text Invalid; text starting with #; leading whitespace other than U+0020; a missing SecTime or BeatTime; values outside -1,000,000 to 1,000,000
marker Id values that are missing, repeated or not decimal integers; content inside WarpMarker; children of WarpMarkers other than WarpMarker
audio clip marker lists with fewer than two markers or not strictly increasing in both positions

code and setting text other than plain decimal digits; codes outside their lists; settings outside their ranges or not integers; IsWarped other than true or false; a missing IsWarped or WarpMode; a TransientEnvelope value other than 100 (every fixture carries 100; the held value is not judged)
children of AudioClip other than those the fixtures carry, other child orders, repeated children

any change to the fixtures' context: the document outside the clip's warp children and marker list, including the clip's sample reference, and the WAV file; any device in a device list (every device list of the fixtures is empty), including a Sampler or Simpler and its sample parts

scripting arguments that are not finite or have magnitude 1,000,000 or more; a move on a list of fewer than three markers; a call that breaks more than one rule, except an add_warp_marker call, which the first failing check of REQ-015 clauses 1 to 5 decides
any other envelope, format version, compressed container or document kind
behavior: everything written on save (REQ-002, 003, 004, 007, 010 save clauses)
an empty marker list, in an audio clip or a sample part (REQ-004); one-marker, out-of-order and equal-position lists (REQ-005); missing or Invalid positions (REQ-006)
the value used, shown and saved for codes and settings outside their ranges (REQ-014); the TransientEnvelope range and default
conversion results after any edit of the clip; conversions on clips that are not audio clips
playback (REQ-009): which sample position plays at a given beat, whether a clip that is not warped uses its warp markers, arrangement clips; the audio output of every warp mode
the default WarpMode of an audio clip and the default warp mode preference
Sampler and Simpler sample parts: where they store warp state (REQ-001 clause 2), their marker lists (REQ-004), codes, settings and defaults; any device in a device list

where and when the application creates or re-places the shadow marker, and the values it gives it; the marker list after an accepted add or remove; move limits and accepted moves; the scripting warp_mode setter; non-audio clips
display of markers, codes, labels and settings; interactive edits, auto-warp, recording and undo
any change the application makes by itself after reading the document, such as automatic warping or sample analysis; whether the original makes one on opening is not established
the structure rules that decide whether a Live Set opens; how a document refers to and finds its sample
refusal presentation and the state after a refusal; error text of scripting calls
